# InfoBadge

Header: `winui/ui/status/InfoBadge.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/status/InfoBadge.hpp`.

A small non-interactive badge showing a number, an icon or a plain dot, typically over a navigation item or a button to flag new or pending items.

What it shows follows [value()](#value) and [icon()](#icon): a value shows the number; otherwise the icon if one is set; otherwise a dot. The fill comes from [severity()](#severity) (the accent by default) unless a local [background()](#background) overrides it. The badge is squared whenever it would be narrower than tall, so a one-digit value is a circle, and its corners are always fully rounded.

Example: 
```cpp
// Declarative: an unread count bound to state, and a critical icon badge.
ui::Property<int> unread{5};
window.set_content(ui::HorizontalStack{
    .spacing  = 8.0f,
    .content  = {
        ui::InfoBadge{.value = unread},
        ui::InfoBadge{
            .severity = ui::InfoBadgeSeverity::Critical,
            .icon     = ui::InfoBadgeControl::severity_glyph(ui::InfoBadgeSeverity::Critical),
        },
    },
});

// Imperative:
auto  stack = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Horizontal);
auto* badge = stack->add(std::make_unique<ui::InfoBadgeControl>(3));
badge->set_severity(ui::InfoBadgeSeverity::Attention);
badge->set_value(std::nullopt); // back to a dot
```

## `ui::InfoBadge`

A small count, icon or dot badge. Builds a [ui::InfoBadgeControl](#uiinfobadgecontrol).

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Property<int> unread{3};

window.set_content(ui::HorizontalStack{
    .spacing  = 8,
    .content  = {
        ui::InfoBadge{.value    = unread},
        ui::InfoBadge{.severity = ui::InfoBadgeSeverity::Critical,
                      .icon     = ui::InfoBadgeControl::severity_glyph(ui::InfoBadgeSeverity::Critical)},
        ui::InfoBadge{}, // a plain dot in the accent color
    },
});
```

```cpp
}
```

```cpp
InfoBadgeControl() = default
```

A dot badge in the Default severity.

### InfoBadgeControl

```cpp
InfoBadgeControl(int value)
```

A badge showing [`value`](#value) (clamped to >= 0).

### value

```cpp
std::optional<int> value() const
```

The number shown; unset (the default) shows the icon, or a dot when there is none.

### set_value

```cpp
void set_value(std::optional<int> value)
```

Sets the number (clamped to >= 0) or clears it. Does nothing if the clamped value is the current one.

### severity

```cpp
InfoBadgeSeverity severity() const
```

Which severity color the fill comes from; Default (the accent) by default.

### set_severity

```cpp
void set_severity(InfoBadgeSeverity severity)
```

Sets the severity; redraws.

### icon

```cpp
const IconSource& icon() const
```

The icon shown while [value()](#value) is unset, sized to the badge: a glyph's code point and font at the badge's glyph size, or a path or picture fitted into the same square.

### set_icon

```cpp
void set_icon(IconSource icon)
```

Sets the icon; an empty source shows the plain dot while [value()](#value) is unset.

### background

```cpp
const std::optional<Color>& background() const
```

A local fixed background, overriding the severity's color. nullopt when there is none or a theme resource is set.

### background_resource

```cpp
ThemeColor background_resource() const
```

The local background as a theme resource, or nullptr.

### set_background

```cpp
void set_background(std::optional<Color> background)
```

Sets or clears the local background and clears a theme-resource one; nullopt goes back to the severity's color. Redraws.

### set_background

```cpp
void set_background(ThemeColor resource)
```

Sets the local background to a theme resource, re-read under every theme, and clears a fixed one. Redraws.

### parallel_measure_safe

```cpp
bool parallel_measure_safe() const override
```

True: measuring reads only the badge's own state, the measurer and the theme.

### automation_role

```cpp
AutomationRole automation_role() const override
```

What screen readers and other assistive tools see of this node: the role, name, help text and children here, and what a client can do with the node through the providers [automation_providers()](../tree/element.md#automation_providers) lists (ui/Automation.hpp).

[automation_role()](#automation_role) is the role this node reports; Group by default.

### automation_name_fallback

```cpp
std::string automation_name_fallback() const override
```

[automation_name()](../tree/element.md#automation_name)'s fallback when [accessibility()](../tree/element.md#accessibility).name is empty. Default: no inherent name, correct for controls with no visible text of their own ([Slider](slider.md#uislider), [ProgressBar](progress-bar.md#uiprogressbar)), which need an explicit [accessibility()](../tree/element.md#accessibility).name from the caller. A control with its own visible text ([Button](button.md#uibutton), [CheckBox](check-box.md#uicheckbox), [TextControl](text.md#uitextcontrol), ...) overrides this to return it.

### severity_glyph

```cpp
static IconGlyph severity_glyph(InfoBadgeSeverity severity)
```

The icon a severity shows: glyphs::InfoBadgeAttention for Attention, glyphs::InfoBarInformational for Informational, and [glyphs::AcceptSymbol](../rendering/namespace-ui-glyphs.md#acceptsymbol), [glyphs::Important](../rendering/namespace-ui-glyphs.md#important) and [glyphs::Cancel](../rendering/namespace-ui-glyphs.md#cancel) for Success, Caution and Critical. `Default` has no icon of its own and gets Attention's.

### measure_override

```cpp
Size measure_override(Size available, const MeasureContext& context) const override
```

Implement these instead of [measure()](../tree/element.md#measure) and [arrange()](../tree/element.md#arrange). The base class has already applied margin, size limits and alignment by the time these run. [measure_override()](#measure_override) is pure (every concrete [Element](../tree/element.md) must size itself); [arrange_override()](../tree/element.md#arrange_override) defaults to a no-op since most leaves need nothing beyond having [bounds()](../tree/element.md#bounds) set, which the base already did.

### render_override

```cpp
void render_override(Renderer& renderer, const RenderContext& context) const override
```

What the control draws, in layout coordinates; [render()](../tree/element.md#render) has already applied the visual layer. A container draws its children through their [render()](../tree/element.md#render), never their [render_override()](#render_override).

## Enumerations

### InfoBadgeSeverity

```cpp
enum class InfoBadgeSeverity
```

The severity a badge takes its background color from.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Default` | the accent fill |
| `Attention` | the attention fill |
| `Informational` | the solid neutral fill |
| `Success` | the success fill |
| `Caution` | the caution fill |
| `Critical` | the critical fill |
